Key classification: 'churn-cancelled-out' means the commit introduces code/files that a LATER commit ANYWHERE in the full range (not just your chunk) deletes again, so the work is absent from the final tree. feat(hybrid): LG1 -- reset-baseline gating for tolerant CSR restores
Profiling hybrid rt_c_hello showed the vsim leg spends 50,394 of its
50,448 simulated cycles on handoff machinery (ROI = 54 cycles), and
~25k of those on one-by-one abstract writes of Andes + M-ext CSRs whose
drained values are still the reset values -- each DM operation costs
~200-900 simulated cycles at ~10 kHz.

ResumeDriver::set_reset_baseline(state) supplies the engine's own
reset-state drain; every write_csr_tolerant site (9 base scalars, the
Andes X-list, PMA, the M-ext X-list) is elided when the drained value
equals the baseline -- the write would be a no-op, so skipping is
verify-transparent and self-heals QEMU-vs-engine reset divergence.
Never gated: mstatus, GPRs, dpc, dcsr, mcycle, minstret, FPR/V blocks
(LG2), S/U PMP mirror. baseline_skip_count() exposes the elision count.

Dormant until LG3 wires a captured baseline in; unset keeps
transport-everything. ROADMAP.md carries the LG1..LG4 plan.

Behavioral.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(hybrid): LG2 -- baseline-elided FPR and V transport blocks
Extend the LG1 reset-baseline gate to the two block transports: the FPR
restore (fld sweep or 32 abstract writes) and the V restore (staging +
vle8 sweep + vsetvl + vstart/vxsat/vxrm/vcsr) are skipped whole when
byte-equal to the engine's reset drain. Profiling hello showed both
blocks fully at reset values yet costing 5,298 + 6,959 simulated cycles
per run.

Clobber rule: the V-data sweep's own vsetvl overwrites vtype/vl/vstart,
so the architectural vsetvl (and the vstart rewrite after it) may only
be elided when the data sweep itself was elided -- baseline equality
compares against the hart AT RESET, which stops holding once a restore
step clobbers a register. Pinned by a dedicated test.

Behavioral.

feat(hybrid): LG3 -- capture + cache the reset baseline; gate is now live
First hybrid run per (engine build, ELF) drains the freshly reset,
just-halted hart into a hybrid_state_v1 baseline and caches it under
$XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim (key: engine name + version + binary mtime/size
+ ELF mtime/size -- the hart free-runs a few workload instructions
before the DMI halt, so the halted state is per-ELF). Later runs load
it and hand it to ResumeDriver::set_reset_baseline, turning the LG1/LG2
liveness gate on for real. --no-reset-baseline restores
transport-everything.

Capture details:
- Runs BEFORE the scratch stagings: its drain sweeps dump reset
  registers through the same scratch page the stagings fill.
- Enables mstatus.FS/VS first (reset leaves them Off, and the fsd/vse8
  capture sweeps -- like resume's own FPR/V writes -- fault with
  cmderr=3 otherwise); resume rewrites mstatus whenever FP/V flags are
  set, so nothing leaks.
- Passes v_cfg_at_reset=false to the gate on capture runs: the capture
  V dump sweep clobbered vtype/vl/vstart, so the vsetvl elision is only
  valid on cache-hit runs (new ResumeDriver param, unit-tested).

Measured on hybrid rt_c_hello (--drain-minimal, ax45mpv_premium): the
vsim leg falls from 50,448 to 12,258 simulated cycles (5.2 s -> 1.15 s;
114 restores elided); whole run 6.4 s -> 1.4 s. Capture run: 59,911
cycles, paid once. --verify passes with the gate active (146 fields).

Behavioral.

feat(hybrid): restore/drain L2C MMIO config via the Program Buffer (ABI v5)
ResumeDriver::restore_l2c writes back the writable boot-static L2C config
registers -- Control (0x0008: CEN enable + prefetch + ECC + RAM timing),
HPM Control (0x0010), Way Allocation Masks (0x0300..) -- as Program-Buffer
word stores (sw, per DS220 11.8.3's <8-byte access rule), staging address
and value in x5/x6 before the GPR loop overwrites them. The read-only
Configuration Register, the side-effecting CCTL command registers
(writing one re-issues an L2 cache op), and the W1C error registers are
never written back. StateDrain::drain_l2c is the dual: lwu (zero-extend)
read-backs of the same registers so --verify compares round-tripped
values instead of the stale QEMU1 passthrough.

Both are HARD-gated on the engine actually having an L2C (set_l2c,
wired from _NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB / _NDS_L2C_REG_BASE -- not the
cluster's has_shared_cache, which also covers L3 on ax46/ax66): unlike
a tolerant CSR write, a PB store to an absent L2C region faults. Every
current engine is built without an L2C, so this is transported
forward-looking and no-ops today.

New encoders encode_sw / encode_lwu (golden hex from riscv64-elf-as)
join the PB toolkit; new recording-bus tests cover the store/read-back
sequences and both gates (flag clear, engine absent).

restore-everything behavior, so existing flows are unchanged. The drain
side stays full-width: re-reading is side-effect-free and records the
engine's true exit values.

CSRs are restored (per-block and per-PMA-entry), and with the flag clear
everything restores as before.
